2c329dd282f4a2b1ffd09599aadb20cb328c2001: Champoluc offers 132 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 21 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the flow in high season. Champoluc has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, unspoilt scenery and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. As for snow, Champoluc is in a strong position with its highest point at 3275 m — even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 1568 m is also well placed to ensure comfortable conditions from mid-December onwards. The budget for a stay in Champoluc is clearly high: 69€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and high-altitude restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you need to be aware of it before you go. In short: Champoluc lives up to its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most profiles without disappointing.

2c7ca93e1cd14d5394aae43608ea55fe0f8c56a7: Val Cenis offers 125 km of well-marked runs, a mid-sized ski area that is ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 29 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Val Cenis's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2800 m and a village at 1400 m, snow reliability at Val Cenis is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. At 50€, the day lift pass places Val Cenis among the mid-range resorts on price: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies the cost for most skiers. In short: Val Cenis is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to have a bad stay here.

2c94a4072071fc239cd9f3ce0712d78b92094468: A resort on a human scale, La Colmiane focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 30 km of runs are perfectly suited to a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. La Colmiane's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Southern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. La Colmiane's modest altitude, with its base at 1,500 m and summit at 1,800 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before departure is strongly recommended. With a day lift pass at just 22€, La Colmiane is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget or skiers who want to get out on the slopes often without breaking the bank, it's a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: La Colmiane doesn't compete with the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
